New course proposals require committee approval and are evaluated on academic merit and student demand. The committee operates by consensus when possible and majority vote when necessary. The dean has rarely overruled committee decisions.

The recycling program was redesigned based on community feedback surveys. The city waste management department proposed three options, hosted public information sessions, and collected comments over 60 days. The final program reflects the most-requested features, though budget constraints meant some popular suggestions couldn't be included.

My graduate program has a clear authority structure. The program director handles admissions and degree requirements. Faculty advisors guide research. The graduate school sets policies that programs must follow. Students have a voice through the graduate student assembly, which meets with the dean monthly.

The nonprofit's executive committee makes decisions between full board meetings. Committee actions must be ratified at the next board meeting. The executive director implements board decisions and manages staff. Staff can propose initiatives through the director, and the board encourages direct communication at annual retreats.

The swim coach sets the training program and meet lineups. Swimmers who disagree with their event assignments can discuss it with the coach, who sometimes adjusts based on their input. The coach is responsive but firm — she knows the sport and parents generally trust her judgment even when their kid isn't swimming their preferred event.

The farmers' market operates under rules set by the market manager and an advisory board of vendors. Rules cover pricing transparency, product standards, and booth assignments. Vendors can propose rule changes at the annual meeting. The manager has day-to-day authority but serves at the board's pleasure.

The clinic's treatment protocols are evidence-based and set by the clinical director. Practitioners follow the protocols as a baseline but can exercise clinical judgment for individual patients. Deviations must be documented and reviewed at the monthly case conference. The system balances standardization with practitioner expertise.

The coworking space has house rules posted in common areas. The community manager enforces them and mediates disputes between members. Major policy decisions are made by the space's owner after consulting the member advisory group. Members can raise issues through a suggestion box that the owner reviews weekly.

The regional planning commission includes representatives from each municipality. Decisions about regional infrastructure require a supermajority vote. Individual municipalities retain local zoning authority but must comply with the regional plan on matters like transportation corridors and watershed protection. It's a balance of local and regional interests.

The expedition leader plans the route, manages safety equipment, and makes all weather-related decisions. Team members choose their own pace within safety parameters and can suggest alternative approaches. In an emergency, the leader's instructions are followed without discussion. Between emergencies, the leadership style is consultative.

The veterans' service organization has a national headquarters that sets policies and a local post commander who runs chapter operations. Members vote on local initiatives and elect their officers annually. National policies can be appealed through a resolution process at the annual convention.

The warehouse supervisor assigns tasks each morning based on order volume and staffing. Workers generally follow their assignments but can swap tasks among themselves with supervisor approval. The supervisor tracks performance metrics but addresses concerns privately rather than publicly. Break times are scheduled but flexible within reason.

The craft guild has a master who oversees quality standards and apprentice training. Journeymen work independently on most projects but consult the master for complex commissions. The guild holds quarterly meetings where all members discuss standards, pricing, and market strategy. Decisions are made by member vote with the master breaking ties.

The apartment building's super handles maintenance and enforces building rules. He reports to the management company but has significant day-to-day authority. Tenants bring concerns to him first. Most issues get resolved informally. For bigger problems, tenants can contact the management company directly or attend the tenant association meetings.

The theater company's producing artistic director selects the season and directs most productions. Guest directors have creative authority over their shows within the company's aesthetic values. The board of directors oversees finances and strategic planning but doesn't interfere with artistic decisions. It's a clear separation of powers.

The immigration case officer reviewed my application and requested additional documentation. The process has clear rules and timelines. I can see my file, respond to concerns, and request a review if denied. It's bureaucratic and slow, but there's a structured process with defined rights for applicants.

The gym's personal trainers design individual programs based on client goals. The gym owner sets general policies about equipment usage and class schedules. Trainers have professional autonomy in their sessions but must follow the gym's safety protocols. Client complaints go to the owner, who mediates when necessary.

The state bar association regulates attorney conduct through published rules and an ethics committee. Complaints go through a formal investigation process. Attorneys have the right to respond, present evidence, and appeal sanctions. The process is adversarial but structured, with due process protections at each stage.

The soccer club's board of directors sets membership fees and facility policies. Coaches are hired by the director of coaching with board input. Parents can serve on committees and vote at the annual general meeting. The club tries to balance competitive goals with inclusivity, and not everyone agrees on the balance.

The senior center's programming is developed by the activities director with input from a resident advisory council. The council meets monthly and suggests activities, outings, and schedule changes. The director accommodates most requests within budget constraints and explains when something isn't feasible.

The open source project has a benevolent dictator model. The maintainer makes final decisions on merges and architecture. Contributors propose changes through pull requests and participate in discussions. The maintainer is responsive to community input and documents reasons for rejecting proposals. Fork rights preserve contributor autonomy.

The daycare center follows state-mandated ratios and curriculum guidelines. Beyond those requirements, the center director has latitude in programming. Teachers plan daily activities within the director's framework. Parents receive regular updates and can discuss concerns at scheduled conferences or through the parent portal.

The credit union is governed by a member-elected board of directors. The CEO manages operations within board-approved policies. Members can attend board meetings, run for board positions, and vote on bylaw changes. Major strategic decisions require a member vote at the annual meeting.

The film set has a strict hierarchy during production. The director calls the shots creatively, the first AD manages the schedule, and department heads run their crews. Between setups, there's more informal collaboration. Safety concerns from any crew member can halt production immediately — that authority isn't hierarchical.

The village council meets monthly to discuss community business. The mayor presides and has a casting vote on tied issues. Council members represent different neighborhoods and are elected every two years. Residents can attend meetings, speak during public comment, and petition for items to be added to the agenda.

The professional development program is structured by the training coordinator but personalized by each employee and their manager. Employees set learning goals, managers approve and fund them, and the coordinator provides resources and tracks completion. It's a three-way partnership with different roles.

The homestead community has shared responsibilities that rotate monthly. A coordinator maintains the schedule and mediates disputes. Major decisions — like adding new members or investing in infrastructure — require unanimous consent. Day-to-day operations follow established protocols that any member can propose to change.

The dental practice has a senior partner who manages the business side and three associate dentists who see patients independently. Clinical decisions are made by the treating dentist. Practice-wide policies on scheduling, insurance, and patient communications are set by the senior partner after discussion at partner meetings.

The historical society's preservation committee reviews all proposed changes to designated landmark properties. Homeowners must submit plans and the committee provides feedback based on published standards. Approved plans include specific conditions. Homeowners who disagree with conditions can appeal to the city council.

The airport's operations are managed by an authority board appointed by the city and county governments. Airlines negotiate gate assignments and service levels within the authority's framework. The airport director handles daily operations. Community advisory boards provide input on noise abatement and expansion plans.

The debate team coach selects which students compete in which events, based on skill assessments and tournament requirements. Students can express preferences and practice for events they're interested in. The coach considers input but makes final roster decisions based on team competitiveness and individual development.

The interfaith council has representatives from each congregation in the community. The council operates by consensus on joint projects like the food pantry and holiday events. No single tradition has veto power. The council chair rotates annually among the participating faith communities.

The summer camp employs a head counselor who manages the counselor team and handles camper behavioral issues. The camp director oversees the head counselor and sets camp-wide policies. Counselors have autonomy in planning their cabin activities within the camp's programming guidelines and safety rules.

The university's financial aid office determines awards based on published criteria. Students can appeal decisions by providing additional documentation. An appeals committee reviews cases and makes recommendations to the financial aid director. The director's decision is final but must be supported by the committee's findings.

My boss and I have a good working relationship. She sets clear expectations and holds me accountable, but she also gives me room to figure out how to meet them. When I disagree with her, she listens. She doesn't always change her mind, but I always feel heard.

The makerspace is run by a volunteer collective with rotating leadership roles. A steering committee handles finances and major decisions. Individual workshop supervisors have authority over safety in their areas. Any member can propose a new workshop or policy change at the monthly meeting.

The insurance commissioner's office regulates health insurance plans in the state. Insurers must submit rate changes for approval and comply with coverage mandates. Consumers can file complaints and request external review of denied claims. The process is regulated with defined rights and procedures for all parties.

The public radio station's programming decisions are made by the program director. The community advisory board meets quarterly and provides feedback on programming. The station manager reports to a board of directors that includes community representatives. During pledge drives, listener preferences visibly influence scheduling.

The roofing company's project foreman directs the crew on each job. The owner bids projects and handles client relations. Workers are expected to follow the foreman's instructions on sequencing and safety. Experienced crew members often mentor newer workers and suggest technique improvements that the foreman usually accepts.

The wilderness therapy program has a structured hierarchy for safety reasons. Field instructors make real-time decisions about group movement and individual interventions. The clinical director provides oversight and treatment planning. Participants have input into their treatment goals and daily routines within the program's therapeutic framework.

The community theater group selects its season through a play-reading committee open to all members. The committee recommends titles and the full membership votes on the final season. Directors are selected by a separate committee. Once cast, the director has creative authority over the production.

The apartment building's management company sends a monthly newsletter with updates on maintenance, policies, and community events. The company maintains a tenant portal for maintenance requests and communication. Building policies are set by the property owner through the management company, but tenants can organize and petition for changes.

The charter school's principal has significant autonomy from the school district in curriculum and staffing decisions. The school's board of directors provides governance oversight. Teachers have more collaborative input here than at traditional schools. Parents choose to enroll their children, which creates accountability through market competition.

The veterinary clinic's owner-veterinarian makes medical decisions on cases she handles. Associate vets handle their own cases independently. The practice manager runs the front office and handles scheduling. Staff meetings happen weekly. Everyone contributes, but the owner has final say on clinic policies.

The state's public utility commission sets electricity rates after public hearings. Utilities propose rates, consumer advocates challenge them, and the commission decides. The process is adversarial but transparent. Ratepayers can attend hearings and submit comments. Decisions can be appealed to state courts.

The co-op grocery store is owned by its members. The board of directors is elected by members and hires the general manager. The manager runs daily operations. Members vote on major decisions at the annual meeting and can serve on committees that advise the board on specific issues.

The nursing unit's charge nurse coordinates patient care during her shift. She assigns patients to nurses based on acuity and staffing. Staff nurses manage their assigned patients independently within the charge nurse's coordination framework. Physicians give medical orders that nurses implement using their clinical judgment.

The county fair 4-H program has leaders who guide young members through their projects. Leaders provide instruction and evaluate projects at fair time. The program coordinator oversees leaders and sets program standards. Parents are involved as helpers. The kids do the work and learn from the structure.

The highway department's chief engineer approves road designs and manages construction contracts. Field inspectors verify contractor compliance. The public can comment on proposed projects during environmental review. Safety concerns raised by any department employee trigger a mandatory review process.

The after-school program coordinator plans activities and supervises staff. The recreation department director sets policies and handles the budget. Kids can suggest activities and vote on certain programming choices. Parents communicate concerns through a parent liaison who attends staff meetings monthly.

The landscaping company's owner designs projects and meets with clients. The crew chief manages daily work assignments and quality. Workers follow the crew chief's direction on planting and maintenance. The owner checks in periodically and handles any client complaints or scope changes.

The assisted living facility has a resident council that meets monthly with the administrator. Residents voice concerns about meals, activities, and policies. The administrator reports back on what changes will be made and explains constraints. The council can't make binding decisions but has real influence on daily operations.

The music festival's booking committee selects performers based on submitted applications and a defined set of criteria. The festival director has oversight and can add featured acts. Local artists have a guaranteed number of slots. Rejected applicants receive feedback and can reapply the following year.

The corporate training department develops programs based on business unit requests and organizational assessments. Department heads can customize content for their teams. Employees provide feedback through post-training surveys. The training director reports to the VP of HR and adjusts programming based on effectiveness data.

The marina's dockmaster assigns slips and enforces boating rules. Slip holders pay fees and follow posted regulations. The marina committee, composed of slip holders, advises the dockmaster on policies. The port authority owns the facility and sets major policies, but daily management is the dockmaster's domain.

The physical therapy practice has a clinical director who sets treatment protocols and supervises staff. Individual therapists adapt protocols to patient needs. Patients are involved in setting their treatment goals and can request changes to their care plan. The director reviews patient outcomes quarterly and adjusts standards accordingly.

The local newspaper's editor assigns stories to reporters based on beats and experience. Reporters pitch story ideas that the editor evaluates for news value. The publisher sets the paper's editorial positions. There's creative tension between journalistic independence and business considerations, but the editor protects the newsroom's integrity.

The heritage preservation society operates through committees for advocacy, education, and fundraising. The board president coordinates between committees. Volunteers self-select into committees based on interest. Major preservation campaigns require board approval. Day-to-day committee work proceeds with considerable autonomy.

The university admissions office uses holistic review with defined criteria. Regional admissions counselors evaluate applications and make recommendations. A committee reviews borderline cases. The dean of admissions makes final decisions on wait-listed applicants. Applicants can supplement their file and appeal denials through a formal process.

The meditation center's teacher leads the practice sessions and gives dharma talks. The center's board manages finances and facilities. Senior students assist with newcomer orientation. Governance decisions are made by the board with teacher input. The teacher has spiritual authority but not organizational authority.

The county extension service employs specialists who provide expertise to farmers. Specialists advise but don't direct — farmers make their own decisions. The county agent coordinates programs and manages the local office. A citizen advisory committee helps set programming priorities based on community agricultural needs.

The conference organizing committee includes volunteers from the professional association. The committee chair assigns sub-committees and coordinates logistics. The association's executive director approves the budget and venue. Presenters are selected through blind peer review. The process is structured but genuinely collaborative.

The volunteer rescue squad operates with an elected chief who directs emergency responses. Members train regularly and follow established protocols. The chief is accountable to the squad's board of directors, which includes community representatives. Operational decisions during calls belong to the chief; governance decisions belong to the board.

The bakery's head baker develops recipes and manages production. The owner handles business operations and customer relations. Staff bakers follow the head baker's instructions on technique and timing. The owner trusts the head baker's expertise and rarely overrides production decisions. It's a small team with clear roles.

The environmental review process requires public notice, a comment period, and agency response to comments. The lead agency prepares the environmental document and makes the final determination. Project opponents can challenge the decision in court. The process balances development interests with environmental protection through structured procedures.

The barbershop has an owner who cuts hair and manages the business. Other barbers rent their chairs and manage their own clients. The owner sets shop hours and house rules. Each barber has autonomy over their service, pricing, and schedule within those parameters. It's a loose but functional hierarchy.

The water district's board of directors sets rates and policies. The general manager oversees staff and operations. Public hearings are required before rate changes. Ratepayers can attend meetings and elect board members. The district operates under state law with oversight from the public utilities commission.

The martial arts dojo has a clear hierarchy of belt ranks. The sensei leads instruction and sets standards for advancement. Senior students help teach junior students. Testing for belt promotion follows published criteria. Students can ask questions and request guidance. The sensei has authority but uses it to develop students, not control them.

The public library system has a director appointed by the library board. Branch managers run their locations with considerable autonomy. Librarians make collection development decisions within board-approved policies. Programming reflects community input gathered through surveys and suggestion boxes. The board sets policy; staff implements it.

The rental property management company responds to maintenance requests within 24 hours for emergencies and 72 hours for routine issues. Tenants can escalate unresolved issues to the property owner. Lease terms are standard but the manager has authority to approve minor accommodations. The relationship is contractual with defined rights.

The tech startup has daily standups where everyone shares what they're working on. The CTO makes technical architecture decisions. Individual developers have significant autonomy in implementation. Product decisions are made collaboratively between the CEO, product manager, and engineering lead. It's hierarchical on paper but relatively flat in practice.

Our housing collective makes all decisions by modified consensus. Any member can block a proposal, but must offer an alternative. We've lived together for five years and this process, while slow, means everyone genuinely supports every decision we make. No one feels steamrolled.

The workers at the brewery voted to convert to an employee-owned cooperative after the founder retired. Every employee-owner has one vote regardless of role or seniority. The board is elected from the membership and the general manager serves at the board's pleasure. Profits are distributed based on hours worked.

Our school uses a democratic governance model where students have genuine decision-making power. The school meeting, which includes every student and staff member with equal votes, sets rules, resolves conflicts, and manages the budget. Staff can be outvoted by students on any matter.

The community mediation center trains volunteers to help neighbors resolve disputes without courts or authority figures. Mediators facilitate but don't decide. Both parties must agree to any resolution. If they can't agree, they leave with the same rights they came in with. Power stays with the people in the room.

The participatory budgeting process gives residents direct control over $2 million in public spending. Anyone over 16 who lives in the district can propose projects, volunteer as a budget delegate, and vote on the final slate. The city council has committed to funding all winning projects.

Our family runs on shared decision-making. Big decisions — moves, major purchases, vacations — get discussed until everyone is comfortable. The kids have genuine input, not just a polite hearing before the adults decide. Sometimes the 12-year-old's argument wins. That's how it should work.

The collective art studio has no director or manager. Members rotate administrative duties monthly. Studio policies, exhibition schedules, and membership decisions are made by consensus at weekly meetings. If someone takes on more responsibility for a project, they gain coordination authority for that project only, not general authority.

The community land trust owns the land and leases it to homeowners at affordable rates. The board has equal representation from residents, community members, and public interest representatives. No single group can dominate. Decisions about land use, affordability requirements, and development require supermajority approval.

Our peer support group has no leader. We rotate the facilitator role each meeting. The facilitator keeps time and ensures everyone has a chance to speak, but doesn't direct the conversation. Group norms were established collectively and can be changed by the group at any time.

The platform cooperative is owned and governed by its users. Drivers, riders, and community stakeholders each elect representatives to the board. Algorithmic decisions — pricing, matching, rating — are transparent and subject to democratic oversight. Workers can't be deactivated without a peer review process.

The restorative justice circle gives equal voice to the person who caused harm, the person who was harmed, and community members. The circle keeper facilitates but has no authority to impose outcomes. The group works together to develop a plan that addresses the harm and meets everyone's needs.

The intentional community uses sociocratic governance. Decisions are made in circles where every member has an equal voice. Consent replaces consensus — objections must be reasoned and related to the proposal's impact on the circle's aims. Authority is distributed through linked circles, not concentrated in individuals.

The tenant union negotiated a collective bargaining agreement with the landlord. Rent increases require 90 days notice and union consultation. Maintenance standards are defined in the agreement. Disputes go to a joint committee with equal tenant and management representation. The union steward has recognized authority to represent tenants.

The cooperative daycare is run entirely by parents. Each family commits to working one shift per week. Administrative duties are shared and rotated quarterly. Major decisions are made at monthly parent meetings by consensus. The hired teacher has authority over pedagogy but parents govern the organization.

The citizen oversight board has subpoena power over the police department. Board members are randomly selected from the community, similar to jury duty. The board reviews complaints, recommends discipline, and publishes findings. Officers subject to investigation have due process rights, but the board's recommendations carry weight.

We restructured our consulting firm as a partnership where every consultant, regardless of tenure, has an equal ownership stake and one vote. We eliminated the managing partner role and replaced it with rotating coordination duties. Compensation is transparent and determined by a formula the whole partnership approved.

The community garden operates on shared governance principles. Plot assignments are made by lottery. Rules about water usage, composting, and shared tool maintenance were developed at a community meeting where every gardener had equal say. The volunteer coordinator serves the community, not the other way around.

The patient advisory council at our clinic has real power, not just an advisory role. Council members participate in hiring decisions, review patient satisfaction data, and help design new services. The clinic director treats council recommendations as binding unless there's a regulatory reason not to follow them.

Our theater ensemble creates all works collaboratively. There is no single director — roles emerge from the devising process. Decisions about the production are made by the whole ensemble. Every member can propose staging ideas, and we work through disagreements by trying each option and evaluating together.

The indigenous governance model in our community integrates traditional authority with modern democratic principles. Elders provide wisdom and cultural continuity. Community assemblies make decisions through extended deliberation. Young people have a dedicated voice through the youth council. No single authority dominates.

The mutual aid network operates without hierarchy. Members offer what they can and request what they need. A rotating coordination team maintains the shared spreadsheet and connects offers with needs. The team has no authority beyond logistics. Trust, not control, holds the network together.

The democratic school lets students design their own learning. There are no required classes, no grades, and no imposed curriculum. Students and staff have equal votes in the school meeting that governs the community. Staff serve as resources and mentors. Students own their education.

We converted our traditional business to a worker-owned cooperative three years ago. Every decision — from hiring to strategic planning — goes through our democratic process. The transition was difficult, but productivity has increased because everyone has a stake in the outcome and a voice in the process.

The neighborhood association uses a town meeting format where every resident can speak and vote. The elected officers handle administrative tasks between meetings but have no independent decision-making authority. Any action that spends money or creates a new rule requires a meeting vote. It's direct democracy at the block level.

The shared workspace is governed by its members. Membership fees are set collectively. The space's rules were drafted at a founding meeting and can be amended by two-thirds vote. There's no owner and no manager — just a member-run operations committee that handles day-to-day logistics.

My therapist emphasizes that our relationship is a genuine partnership. She brings expertise, I bring self-knowledge. Treatment goals are set together. She never imposes a direction — she offers perspectives and I decide what resonates. If I disagree with an approach, we find one that works for both of us.

The community health clinic is governed by a board where the majority must be active patients. This ensures the people who use the services shape the policies. Staff report to a director who reports to the patient-majority board. It's a genuine power-sharing model that centers the community.

The food cooperative's bylaws ensure that no single person or group accumulates disproportionate power. The board is term-limited. Committee chairs rotate. The general membership votes on all major decisions. Even the general manager can be recalled by a member petition and vote.

Our classroom operates as a community of learners. Students and I develop the class norms together at the start of each semester. Assessment criteria are transparent and co-developed. Students can propose alternative assignments that meet the learning objectives. My role is to facilitate, not dictate.

The renewable energy cooperative is owned by the households it serves. Members elect the board, vote on rate structures, and receive patronage dividends. The cooperative's general manager is accountable to the board. Energy sourcing decisions — solar, wind, biomass — are made by member referendum.

The youth council in our city has a real budget and real authority over youth programming. Council members are elected by their peers. They allocate funds, hire program staff, and evaluate outcomes. Adult advisors provide guidance but cannot override council decisions. Young people govern young people's resources.

Our recovery house operates on peer governance. House meetings are held weekly where all residents have equal voice. House rules can be amended by majority vote. Peer accountability replaces top-down enforcement. A rotating house coordinator handles logistics but has no authority beyond coordination.

The online community forum is moderated by elected moderators who serve six-month terms. Moderation guidelines were developed through community discussion and are publicly documented. Any moderation action can be appealed to a community review panel. Moderator elections are open to all active community members.

The neighborhood tool library runs on trust and mutual respect. Any resident can borrow tools. There's no check-out system — just a sign-up sheet and a shared understanding that tools get returned in working condition. Volunteers maintain the collection. Decisions about new acquisitions are made at open monthly meetings.

The conflict resolution team uses a circle process where everyone affected by a decision sits together as equals. There's no judge, no authority figure making the call. The circle keeper ensures everyone is heard. Solutions emerge from the group. Agreements are voluntary and collaborative.

We abolished the executive director position and replaced it with a leadership collective. Four staff members share administrative responsibilities and rotate the external-facing roles. Major decisions require all four to agree. It's less efficient but ensures no single person controls the organization.

The parents in our homeschool cooperative each teach a subject based on their expertise. Families contribute equally to planning, logistics, and costs. Curriculum decisions are made collaboratively. If a family disagrees with an approach, we find an alternative together. No single family dominates the direction.

The disability rights organization is led by people with disabilities. The board, staff, and volunteers are all drawn from the disability community. 'Nothing about us without us' isn't a slogan here — it's a governance requirement. People affected by policies make the policies.

Our condominium association eliminated the board president position and now operates with co-chairs who rotate quarterly. All policy decisions go to a full owner vote. The property manager executes decisions but cannot make policy independently. We designed the system to prevent the power concentration we experienced under the previous board.

The community radio station's programming is determined by its members. Volunteer programmers have creative control over their shows within community-developed guidelines. The station's board is elected by dues-paying members. Budget priorities are set at the annual meeting. Corporate underwriting doesn't influence content.

The cohousing community makes all decisions by consensus at community meetings. Every household has an equal voice. Work responsibilities are shared through committees that any member can join. There's no president or director — just facilitators who rotate and serve the process.

The employee-owned cleaning cooperative sets wages, schedules, and work standards collectively. New clients and pricing are approved by member vote. Each worker-owner has one share and one vote regardless of tenure. The elected coordinator handles scheduling and client communication but doesn't have managerial authority over other worker-owners.

The community justice center uses a peer court model where trained community volunteers hear cases referred by the justice system. Volunteers and participants sit together as equals. Outcomes focus on accountability and restoration, not punishment. The process gives community members genuine authority in their own justice system.

Our research lab runs on a flat structure. The PI sets the broad research agenda, but individual researchers design and execute their own projects. Lab meetings are collaborative brainstorming sessions, not progress reports. Publishing decisions are made together. Everyone's name goes on papers they contributed to, in order of contribution.

The free clinic is staffed entirely by volunteers who rotate roles. Physicians, nurses, and administrators share governance equally through a steering committee. Clinical protocols are evidence-based and collaboratively developed. No single volunteer has permanent authority — influence comes from expertise and contribution, not position.

The children's council at our school meets weekly to discuss issues that affect student life. Teachers attend as observers but can only speak when invited. The council's decisions about recess activities, lunch options, and classroom norms are implemented by the school. Children experience real democratic participation.

The immigrant mutual aid society is run by and for immigrants. Leadership rotates among cultural communities. Decisions about resource allocation are made at multi-lingual assemblies. Professional service providers serve as consultants to the community, not as authorities over it. The community defines its own needs.

The technology cooperative develops open-source tools owned collectively by its member-developers. Technical decisions are made through a request-for-comment process open to all members. Revenue from services is distributed according to a formula the membership approved. The cooperative has no CEO — governance is through elected, rotating committees.

Our family meetings happen every Sunday. Everyone, including the youngest, gets to put items on the agenda and has a vote. We've made real decisions this way — where to donate money, whether to get a pet, how to divide chores. The parents don't have veto power.

The fisheries cooperative manages the local catch sustainably. Every fishing family has one vote. Catch limits, pricing, and market access decisions are made at quarterly assemblies. The cooperative's manager handles logistics and sales but reports to the membership. Profits are shared based on catch contribution.
